title: Oracle Manipulation and Stale Data
learning_outcomes: Explain Oracle Manipulation and Stale Data and relate it to the contract execution model.
Analyze or implement a small Solidity example involving Oracle Manipulation and Stale Data.

content.intro: This lesson turns the syllabus topic “Oracle Manipulation and Stale Data” into a small, inspectable example. You will work from an expected behavior, run a local check, and record the assumptions behind the result.
content.why_it_matters: Start with a threat model: identify who controls each input, who may call the function, what external code can do, and what happens when a call fails. Demonstrate the expected behavior and a denied or adversarial case in a controlled local test.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Security starts with a threat model and explicit trust boundaries. Enforce authorization, validate inputs, minimize external-call risk, and use adversarial local tests.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: 1. Predict how the example should behave in relation to Oracle Manipulation and Stale Data. 2. Compile it with the pinned compiler and inspect warnings. 3. Test one normal case and one boundary or failure case in a local EVM. 4. Record what the result demonstrates and what it does not establish about production safety.

content_blocks.expected_output: isFresh(updatedAt) returns true only when the supplied timestamp is not in the future and is less than one hour old.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a local EVM test environment and pin the compiler, EVM target, optimizer settings, and tool versions. This is static lesson content; CodeLeaf does not run arbitrary Solidity in the web app. Do not test contracts or vulnerabilities on systems you do not own or have permission to assess.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Reset the local VM or restart the test fixture, redeploy the example, and repeat the same tests. Restore the original compiler, optimizer, and EVM-target settings before comparing results. Never add keys or other secrets to source files.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: A snippet that compiles is not automatically correct or secure. Check the selected compiler version, read every warning, assert preconditions, test reverting and edge cases, and inspect external-call assumptions. If a tool or opcode is unsupported, verify the compiler release and target-chain support instead of weakening checks.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the small example to demonstrate Oracle Manipulation and Stale Data. Write down the expected result before running it, add a normal test and a failure/boundary test, then note one design trade-off or security concern.

content_blocks.title: Recap and next step
content_blocks.text: Recap: Oracle Manipulation and Stale Data should be understood alongside the module principle: Security starts with a threat model and explicit trust boundaries. Enforce authorization, validate inputs, minimize external-call risk, and use adversarial local tests. Continue to the next lesson only after you can explain the behavior, reproduce the result locally, and state the important limitations.

content.task: Create a small local-only example that demonstrates Oracle Manipulation and Stale Data. Define a normal case and a boundary/failure case, predict the result, test both, and explain one limitation. Do not deploy this teaching exercise with real funds.
task_acceptance_criteria: State the expected behavior before testing and describe the observed result.
Include a repeatable test or manual trace covering a boundary or failure case.
Document one assumption, security concern, or version constraint rather than claiming production readiness.
hints: Start with the simplest behavior related to Oracle Manipulation and Stale Data and make the input and expected result explicit.
Change one condition or input at a time and rerun the same test to isolate the effect.
Read compiler warnings and error details; do not treat deployment success as a security review.
content.expected_output: isFresh(updatedAt) returns true only when the supplied timestamp is not in the future and is less than one hour old.
troubleshooting: Confirm that the compiler version is 0.8.37 and that build settings are recorded.
For a revert, inspect the precondition and test both allowed and denied inputs.
For external calls or network-specific features, confirm the local chain's behavior and the target-network assumptions.
